patients.summary: Long-haul truck driver and heavy smoker who joins in 2022 with knee osteoarthritis, chronic bronchitis, constipation and mild iron deficiency anemia. A right lower lobe adenocarcinoma is found in 2023 after he defers screening and then bronchoscopy; stage IIIB, treated with chemoradiation in 2024, complicated by TRALI during a transfusion for anemia, then sigmoid diverticulitis in 2025 and Guillain-Barré syndrome in 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
56M establishing care, transferring from his prior primary care office. Long-haul truck driver, usually out Wed-Sat.

PMH (per pt, prior records requested):
- Chronic constipation for years. Metamucil packet daily, MiraLAX when he gets backed up on the road. Gets maybe 3 BMs/week when driving, better at home.
- Bilateral knee OA. Worse climbing in and out of the cab. Takes ibuprofen 400 mg most days, sometimes 2-3x/day on long runs.
- Chronic bronchitis. Morning productive cough most days, albuterol a few times a week, more in cold weather.
- Iron deficiency anemia, told about it last year by prior PCP, told to cut back on Advil-type pills. Never took iron.
- Tobacco: started at 20, about a pack and a half a day now, ~40 pack-years. Tried OTC patches this spring for a few weeks, went back. Thinking about a quit-smoking group at a community health center this fall.
PSH: none.
Meds: psyllium 3.4 g daily; ibuprofen 400 mg q6-8h prn knees; albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4-6h prn wheeze; PEG 3350 17 g daily prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father had lung cancer, diagnosed at 62, died of it. Mother has diverticulosis. Maternal uncle had Guillain-Barré after an infection.
SH: lives in Leeds. Drinks 1-2 beers on weekends only. No drugs.

ROS: chronic AM cough, no hemoptysis, no weight change he has noticed, no chest pain, no melena or blood in stool. Knees ache, no locking.

Exam: Well-appearing, smells of smoke. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no LAD. Lungs: no wheeze or crackles, good air movement. CV regular, no murmur. Abd soft, NT, no masses. Knees: no effusion, no warmth, full ROM with discomfort at end flexion. No edema. Skin normal.

A/P:
1. Tobacco use - discussed at length; he wants to try the group on his own schedule. Not interested in Rx today. Eligible for lung cancer screening (56, 40 pk-yr, current smoker) - LDCT ordered, explained it is a yearly low-dose scan. He will call radiology to schedule around his runs.
2. Chronic bronchitis - continue albuterol prn.
3. Knee OA - discussed limiting ibuprofen given anemia history; take with food, lowest dose that works.
4. Constipation - continue fiber + PEG prn.
5. IDA - CBC, iron studies today.
6. HCM - CMP, lipids, A1c, HCV and HIV screens today. Tdap and PCV20 given. Flu/COVID/Shingrix at a nurse visit next month when the fall vaccines are in. Colonoscopy per prior records (pending).
RTC 6 months, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Hickey - your labs are back. Your hemoglobin is at the low end of normal and your iron stores are low, which fits the iron deficiency your last doctor found. It's mild. The best thing for it is cutting down the ibuprofen as we talked about. Kidney and liver tests, cholesterol and sugar (A1c) look fine. Hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Have a safe trip.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received 14 pages by fax from patient's previous primary care office, covering 2016-2022. Abstracted:
- 04/2021 routine labs: mild anemia, low ferritin. Assessed as iron deficiency from chronic NSAID use. Advised to reduce ibuprofen. No iron prescribed.
- 06/2021 screening colonoscopy (age 54): normal to the cecum, no polyps. Repeat in 10 years.
- Problem list on their end: knee OA, chronic bronchitis, constipation, tobacco use, anemia.
- Med list matches what patient reported here.
- Vaccines: no record of Tdap or pneumococcal.
Scanned to media tab. Colonoscopy entered in health maintenance, next due 2031.

documents.title: Office Visit - tobacco
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here to talk about smoking, which we set up last fall. Over the last year he has tried to stop twice. Spring 2022 with OTC nicotine patches, then in the fall the group program at the community health center. Each time he made it several weeks. Both times the cravings came back hard when work got stressful (tight delivery windows, nights in the truck) and he was back to a pack and a half a day. He is clear that he knows it's bad for him, especially with the bronchitis. But today: "I'm not ready to go at it again right now. Maybe someday."

We spent most of the visit on what matters to him. He brought up his father, who smoked and died of lung cancer in his 60s. He wants to keep driving till he can retire on his terms. Smoking is tied up with staying awake on long hauls and with the breaks at truck stops. Asked what would need to be different for a third try to stick; he said a slower stretch at work, and maybe something for the cravings that isn't a patch. I told him the decision is his and the door is open whenever he wants; we can talk about varenicline or bupropion when he's ready. He did not want a prescription today.

Asked again about the lung screening CT - still not done. He would rather do it when he has a week off in the summer. Reviewed why it matters with his history.

Other: knees same, still on ibuprofen most days. Bowels OK with fiber. Cough unchanged, his usual morning cough.
Meds/allergies reviewed, NKDA. FH unchanged.

O: vitals reviewed. Comfortable, NAD. Lungs without wheeze. Heart regular.

A/P:
- Tobacco use disorder, precontemplation-to-contemplation. Autonomy-supportive conversation; no drug started. Revisit each visit.
- Lung cancer screening - LDCT order still open, he will schedule in summer.
- Shingrix #2 given today.
RTC 6 mo.

documents.title: Knees
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Knees have been rough the last couple weeks, lot of loading and unloading on this route. Taking the ibuprofen 3 times a day. Is that ok for a while or is there something better

documents.title: RE: Knees
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry the knees are acting up. Short stretches of ibuprofen three times a day with food are OK, but please don't keep it up for weeks given your iron levels - it can irritate the stomach and cause slow blood loss. Ice after a long day helps. If it's not settling in two weeks, come in and we can look at other options, including an injection.

orders.reason: Chronic cough with unintentional weight loss, 40 pack-year smoker

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: cough, weight loss

S: The cough has been worse for several months - more of it, through the day now, not just mornings. He figured it was his bronchitis and kept using the albuterol, but it hasn't let up, which is why he came in. He's also lost weight without trying; belt is a notch tighter. Appetite so-so. No fevers. Denies blood in sputum. Still 1.5 ppd. Never got to the screening CT.

O: Wt 99.5 kg, down from 103 last fall. Afebrile. Lungs: no wheeze, no focal findings I can appreciate. No clubbing noted. No LAD.

A/P: Persistent cough + unintentional weight loss in a 56 y/o with 40 pack-years and a father with lung cancer. This needs a real workup, not a screening scan - cancelling the LDCT order and sending him to pulmonology for evaluation and imaging. Asked them to see him soon. CBC/CMP today. Talked frankly about what we are looking for; he understands. Will call him when the referral is scheduled.

conditions.label: Suspected malignant neoplasm of lung
conditions.note: 3.5 cm RLL mass on CT, tissue diagnosis pending.

reports.text:
CT CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST
Indication: Chronic cough, weight loss, heavy smoking history.
Technique: Axial images from the thoracic inlet through the upper abdomen after IV contrast; coronal and sagittal reformats.
Findings: Right lower lobe mass measuring 3.5 cm in greatest dimension on axial images. Airways otherwise patent. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No acute osseous abnormality.
reports.conclusion: 3.5 cm right lower lobe mass, suspicious for primary lung malignancy. Tissue sampling recommended.

documents.title: Pulmonology consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 09/05/2023

Dear Doctor,
Thank you for sending Mr. Hickey, 56, for evaluation of persistent cough and weight loss.

He has coughed for years and carries a label of chronic bronchitis. Over the past several months the cough has become constant and he has lost weight without trying. He assumed it was more of the same bronchitis and only came in because it would not ease up. Current smoker, about 40 pack-years. Father died of lung cancer. Works as a long-haul driver.
Medications: psyllium daily, ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for knees (uses it most days), albuterol as needed, MiraLAX as needed. NKDA.

Imaging: CT chest obtained today is positive - a 3.5 cm right lower lobe mass.

Impression: On his risk factors alone (age, heavy ongoing smoking, first-degree relative) I would have put his chance of a lung cancer at around 30% before imaging. A CT showing a mass of this kind moves that substantially higher; I think it is more likely than not that this is a primary lung cancer, and it needs tissue.

Plan:
1. Bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound for sampling of the mass and nodal staging - our scheduler will contact him.
2. Continue albuterol as needed.
3. Smoking cessation strongly advised.
I will write again once we have pathology.

Pulmonary and Critical Care
Allergies: NKDA

Explained the CT finding needs a biopsy and delays matter. He'll call pulmonology to rebook for October. Routed to PCP.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pulmonology let us know he cancelled the rebooked bronchoscopy (10/19). Called him. He is coughing more, says he's been putting it off because he doesn't want to hear it. I told him plainly that the mass on the CT is very likely cancer, that finding out sooner gives him more options, and that I'd help him clear the time. He listened. Says he will talk to his dispatcher about taking two weeks in November. Will see him in clinic in November regardless; front desk to book.

orders.reason: Right lower lobe lung mass, worsening symptoms, weight loss

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Last three months the breathing has gotten worse - winded walking across the truck stop lot. Cough constant, and the last few weeks he's seen streaks of blood in the sputum now and then. Losing weight. Albuterol not helping much. He has not had the bronchoscopy. He's scared and says he's ready to deal with it now; he's taken the next two weeks off.
Still smoking about 1.5 ppd.

O: Wt 91 kg (99.5 in Aug). Looks tired, thinner in the face. Speaking full sentences. Lungs: no wheeze; nothing focal on my exam. Heart regular. No LAD in neck.

A/P: RLL mass on CT in Sept, now with hemoptysis, dyspnea and 8+ kg weight loss, no tissue diagnosis yet. Spoke directly with the hematology-oncology office - they'll see him within two weeks and coordinate bronchoscopy from there. Urgent referral placed. He agrees. Reviewed ED precautions for heavy bleeding or bad shortness of breath. Will touch base after his oncology visit.

reports.text: PA and lateral views of the chest. Mass in the right lower lobe. Heart size within normal limits. No pneumothorax. Bones intact.

CT CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST
Comparison: CT chest 09/05/2023.
Findings: Right lower lobe mass now measures 4.0 cm in greatest axial dimension (previously 3.5 cm). Associated mediastinal lymphadenopathy. No pleural effusion. Heart and great vessels normal in caliber. Imaged upper abdomen unremarkable. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: 4 cm right lower lobe mass with associated lymphadenopathy, enlarged since 09/2023. Findings concerning for primary lung carcinoma with nodal involvement.

documents.title: Hematology & Oncology new patient consultation
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 12/11/2023

Reason: right lower lobe lung mass.

History: 57-year-old man with tobacco use disorder, chronic bronchitis, knee osteoarthritis, constipation and iron deficiency anemia, seen in pulmonology in September for cough and weight loss with a positive chest CT. Bronchoscopy was booked but not done. Since then, three months of increasing shortness of breath, ongoing cough with intermittent blood-streaked sputum, and 10 kg of weight loss he cannot explain, despite continuing his usual bronchitis treatment. No recent travel, no sick contacts.
Family: father with lung cancer.
Social: smokes, 40 pack-years. Long-haul driver.
Medications: psyllium daily, ibuprofen 400 mg PRN (chronic), albuterol PRN, MiraLAX PRN. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Weight 89 kg. Thin. Hypertrophic changes of the skin and nails with clubbing of the fingers. Decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion at the right lung base. Heart regular. Abdomen benign. No palpable lymphadenopathy.

Data today: Hgb 13.5 g/dL (slightly low), WBC 7.5, platelets 250. Na 140, K 4.2, Ca 10.2 (upper limit of normal), alk phos 120 (normal). CEA elevated.
Chest radiograph shows a right lower lobe mass; CT the same afternoon shows the mass at 4 cm with associated lymph node enlargement.

Assessment: Presentation highly suspicious for non-small cell lung cancer with nodal disease.
Plan: EBUS bronchoscopy with sampling of mass and nodes, arranged with interventional pulmonology for 12/19. PET-CT and brain MRI for staging. Return after pathology.

Hematology & Oncology

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of lung
conditions.note: Adenocarcinoma, right lower lobe, mediastinal nodes positive.

reports.text:
SPECIMENS: (A) Right lower lobe mass, EBUS-guided transbronchial needle aspiration and core. (B) Mediastinal lymph node, EBUS-TBNA.
MICROSCOPIC: (A) Malignant glandular epithelium infiltrating fibrous stroma. Immunostains: TTF-1 positive, napsin A positive, p40 negative. (B) Lymphoid tissue with metastatic carcinoma of the same morphology.
Molecular testing sent.
reports.conclusion: (A) Adenocarcinoma, consistent with lung primary. (B) Mediastinal lymph node positive for metastatic adenocarcinoma.

documents.title: Bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PROCEDURE REPORT, received 12/22/2023
Date of procedure: 12/19/2023
Procedure: flexible bronchoscopy with linear EBUS, transbronchial needle sampling of right lower lobe mass and mediastinal lymph node.
Anesthesia: moderate sedation. Airway inspection: no endobronchial lesion seen. Samples obtained with rapid on-site evaluation showing malignant cells. Estimated blood loss minimal. No complications; discharged home same day.
Pathology (finalized 12/21): adenocarcinoma of lung origin; sampled mediastinal node positive. Molecular studies pending.
Allergies: NKDA. Copy to primary care and hematology-oncology.

documents.title: Call to patient - pathology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Phil after the pathology came through. Oncology had already told him on Wednesday - adenocarcinoma, lymph node involved. He was quieter than usual but asked good questions: whether it had spread (staging scans set for 1/3 and 1/4), whether he can keep working (one step at a time). Asked how he is coping - says he isn't sleeping much. Offered to see him before treatment starts and he accepted; front desk to book early January. Reminded him we're reachable by phone or portal anytime.

documents.title: Oncology staging summary and treatment plan
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 01/08/2024

Re: Philip Hickey, 57

Diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the right lower lobe of the lung, mediastinal nodal involvement on EBUS (12/19/2023).

Staging:
- PET-CT 01/03/2024: FDG-avid right lower lobe mass and FDG-avid mediastinal nodes. No FDG-avid disease outside the chest.
- MRI brain with and without contrast 01/04/2024: no intracranial metastatic disease.
- Molecular profiling of the tumor: no EGFR mutation, no ALK rearrangement.
Clinical stage IIIB. Reviewed at our thoracic tumor board: not a surgical candidate given the nodal disease; recommendation is definitive concurrent chemoradiation.

Plan: weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel given with thoracic radiation, 60 Gy in 30 fractions, start 01/22/2024. Radiation oncology simulation done 01/10. Weekly labs during treatment. We discussed goals - treatment is given with curative intent.

We strongly encouraged him to stop smoking; he is not ready to commit.
Medications: psyllium, ibuprofen PRN, albuterol PRN, polyethylene glycol PRN. Allergies: NKDA.

Hematology & Oncology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to check in before chemoradiation starts on the 22nd. Staging done - stage IIIB adenocarcinoma RLL, no spread outside the chest on PET, brain MRI clear, no EGFR/ALK. Plan is weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel with 6 weeks of radiation, curative intent. He has met radiation oncology.

How he's doing: sleeping a little better since he has a plan. Breathing about the same as November. Cough, occasional blood streaks, no big bleeds. Appetite fair.
Smoking: still about 1.5 ppd. We talked about how stopping now could help him get through radiation. Offered varenicline, nicotine replacement, or a referral to the cancer center's tobacco program. He says he can't take on one more thing this month. Will ask again.

Vitals reviewed, weight stable since oncology visit. Lungs: no wheeze, no increased work of breathing. Heart regular.

A/P:
- Lung adenocarcinoma, stage IIIB - treatment per oncology. Asked him to keep us posted, and to message for anything non-cancer.
- Constipation - chemo antiemetics can make it worse; keep fiber going and use MiraLAX daily if needed.
- Knees - ibuprofen sparingly during chemo; check with oncology about using it.
- Tobacco - declines a medication today.
RTC 2 months or sooner.

documents.title: Bowels
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Halfway through the radiation. Bowels are slow again, 4 days no BM. Can I take more of the MiraLAX

documents.title: RE: Bowels
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Mr. Hickey, yes - you can take the MiraLAX every day, even twice a day for a day or two until things move, then back to once daily. Keep up the fluids and the Metamucil. If you have belly pain, vomiting, or still nothing after 2 more days, call us or your oncology team.

documents.title: Radiation oncology treatment summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
RADIATION ONCOLOGY END-OF-TREATMENT SUMMARY
Patient: Philip Hickey
Diagnosis: right lower lobe lung adenocarcinoma, stage IIIB
Course: thoracic radiation, 60 Gy in 30 fractions, 01/22/2024 through 03/01/2024, with weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel given by medical oncology. All fractions delivered, no treatment breaks.
Tolerance: fatigue, expected.
Follow-up: restaging CT chest in about 5 weeks with medical oncology; radiation oncology visit in 3 months.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:

Smoking: still smoking daily. Not ready for a med.
Restaging CT with oncology early April.

CT CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST

reports.conclusion: Treatment response: right lower lobe mass decreased to 2.6 cm. No new disease.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 05/17/2024  Discharged: 05/21/2024
Service: Hematology/Oncology

Principal problem: symptomatic anemia during chemotherapy, complicated by transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI).

History: 57-year-old man with stage IIIB right lower lobe adenocarcinoma diagnosed in December, treated with concurrent chemoradiation and now on consolidation carboplatin/paclitaxel (cycle 2 on 05/06). About a month of increasing fatigue and shortness of breath. Takes ibuprofen chronically for knee osteoarthritis. Known iron deficiency anemia. Admitted for evaluation of worsening anemia.

Course: Hemoglobin 7.4 g/dL with MCV 78 fL on arrival. Given IV fluids, then started on packed red blood cells. About 2 hours into the transfusion he developed chills and discomfort. T 38.5 C, HR 102, BP 124/78, SpO2 98% on room air. At that point he denied back pain, dark urine, rash or trouble breathing. Exam: pale conjunctivae, mild tachycardia. Transfusion was stopped and the blood bank notified; direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test negative.
Over the next two hours his oxygen saturation fell to 86% on room air with respiratory rate 28. Portable chest film showed new bilateral infiltrates; NT-proBNP 180 pg/mL, no clinical volume overload. Diagnosed with TRALI and reported to the blood bank. Supported with nasal cannula oxygen up to 5 L/min; he did not need intubation. Weaned to room air by 05/19. Repeat film 05/20 showed the infiltrates clearing.
Anemia: ferritin 6 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 4% - iron deficiency, most likely from chronic NSAID use, with chemotherapy contributing. Ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg IV given 05/20; second 750 mg dose scheduled at the infusion center 05/28. Ibuprofen stopped. Hemoglobin 7.9 at discharge.

Discharge medications: psyllium daily; albuterol HFA PRN; polyethylene glycol 3350 PRN. STOP ibuprofen.
Allergies: NKDA. Add to record: history of TRALI - transfusion medicine consult before any future transfusion.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week; oncology 06/10. No further chemotherapy cycles planned at this time.

medications.sig: Take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for knee pain. Max 3,000 mg per day.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital 5/17-5/21 for anemia (Hgb 7.4) on consolidation chemo. Reaction to the blood transfusion with fever then low oxygen and bilateral infiltrates - TRALI. Needed oxygen for 2 days, no ICU, no intubation. IV iron in the hospital, second dose at the infusion center this morning. Discharge summary reviewed and meds reconciled.

Today: breathing back to his usual. No fever. Still tired. Knees are bothering him off the ibuprofen.

Vitals reviewed, SpO2 normal on RA. Wt 86 kg. Pale but less so per him. Lungs: no crackles, no wheeze. Heart regular, no edema.
CBC in clinic: Hgb 9.4 - up from 7.9 at discharge.

A/P:
1. TRALI - resolved clinically. Added to his record; any future transfusion needs a transfusion medicine review first.
2. Iron deficiency anemia - improving with IV iron. Recheck CBC and iron in 6-8 weeks.
3. Knee OA - no more ibuprofen or other NSAIDs. Start acetaminophen 500 mg, 1-2 every 6 hours as needed, no more than 3 g a day. Ice, and we can revisit an injection when he's further from chemo.
4. Lung cancer - oncology 6/10 to decide next steps.
5. Tobacco - still smoking. Offered help again; not yet.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 06/10/2024

Stage IIIB RLL adenocarcinoma, s/p concurrent chemoradiation (completed 03/01/2024) and two consolidation cycles of carboplatin/paclitaxel. Admission in May for anemia complicated by TRALI; recovered.
We discussed consolidation durvalumab. Given the recent lung injury and the risk of immune pneumonitis in the treated lung, we have elected not to start it. He agrees.
Treatment is complete. Surveillance: CT chest every 3-4 months for 2 years, then less often. Next CT in August.
Anemia improving on IV iron. Off NSAIDs.
Allergies: NKDA. History of TRALI.
Hematology & Oncology

documents.title: Blood count and iron
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news - your hemoglobin is up to 12.5 and your iron stores are refilled after the IV iron. No more iron needed right now. Stay off the ibuprofen and we'll recheck at your physical in September.

documents.title: RE: Blood count and iron
documents.author: patient
documents.body: great thanks. feeling a lot more like myself

58M, annual exam.

Interval: stage IIIB RLL adenocarcinoma, chemoradiation Jan-Mar, 2 consolidation cycles, admission in May for anemia with TRALI. Treatment done, surveillance CTs with oncology; August CT showed further shrinkage, nothing new.
Feels well. Appetite good, weight coming back (91 kg). Cough at baseline. No hemoptysis since spring. Knees manageable with acetaminophen; has not been taking ibuprofen. Bowels OK with fiber, MiraLAX now and then.
Smoking: still daily, about the same amount. He knows. Said he'd think about varenicline after the holidays.
Alcohol: a couple beers on weekends.

Meds: psyllium daily, acetaminophen PRN, albuterol PRN, PEG PRN.
Allergies: NKDA. History of TRALI (transfusion).

Exam: Well. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Lungs without wheeze or crackles. Heart regular, no murmur. Abd soft, NT. Knees no effusion. Ext no edema. Skin intact.

A/P:
- Health maintenance: colonoscopy 2021 normal, next 2031. Tdap 2022. PCV20 done. Shingrix complete. Flu + COVID next month at nurse visit. HCV/HIV done 2022.
- Labs today: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c.
- Lung cancer - surveillance with oncology.
- IDA - recheck Hgb today; avoid NSAIDs.
- Tobacco - 2 minutes on cessation; not ready, open to revisiting in January.
RTC 4-5 months.

reports.text:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST
Indication: LLQ pain, fever.
Findings: Sigmoid colon diverticula with wall thickening and surrounding fat stranding centered on the sigmoid. No abscess. No free air. No free fluid. Liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, adrenal glands and kidneys unremarkable. Appendix normal. Bladder unremarkable. No lymphadenopathy. Imaged lung bases with post-radiation change at the right base. No osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Acute uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis. No abscess or perforation.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Visit 05/06/2025

CC: left lower abdominal pain x2 days.
HPI: 58M, stage IIIB lung cancer treated last year, history of TRALI. Two days of left lower quadrant pain, came on acutely, constant and sharp, worse when he moves or goes over bumps. Felt feverish. No vomiting. No blood per rectum.
Meds: fiber supplement daily, MiraLAX as needed, albuterol inhaler as needed; occasional ibuprofen for knee pain.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother with diverticulosis. Father with lung cancer.
Social: smoker, 40 pack-years. Diet mostly red meat, few fruits or vegetables. Truck driver.

Exam: T 38.3 C, HR 102, BP 135/85. BMI 32. Uncomfortable. Abdomen: LLQ tenderness with guarding, no rebound. Rectal: no blood.
Labs: WBC 14.0, Hgb 13.8, CRP 24 mg/L (ref <5).
CT A/P: acute uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis, no abscess or perforation.

MDM: uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis. Tolerating PO, pain controlled after IV fluids and acetaminophen. Will treat as outpatient with antibiotics given fever and leukocytosis.
Disposition: home. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID x7 days. Clear liquids advancing to low-residue diet for a few days. Avoid NSAIDs. PCP follow-up this week. Return for worsening pain, persistent fever, vomiting, or bleeding.

reports.text: Motor nerve conduction studies of the upper and lower limbs show prolonged distal latencies, slowed conduction velocities and prolonged or absent F waves. Sensory responses reduced in the upper limbs with relative sparing of the sural responses. Needle EMG of selected limb muscles shows reduced recruitment without active denervation.
reports.conclusion: Acute demyelinating sensorimotor polyneuropathy, consistent with acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (Guillain-Barré syndrome).

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 05/07/2026 (neuro ICU)  Discharged: 05/15/2026 to inpatient rehabilitation
Service: Neurology

Principal diagnosis: Guillain-Barré syndrome, acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy.

History: 59-year-old man with stage IIIB NSCLC treated with chemoradiation and chronic bronchitis, last seen in our system in 2025 for diverticulitis. Three days of tingling in both feet that climbed to weakness in both legs, then his hands felt weak, with mild shortness of breath. He had been treated for a respiratory infection about two weeks before.
Family: maternal uncle had post-infectious Guillain-Barré. Father, lung cancer. Mother, diverticulosis.
Social: smoker, 40+ pack-years; occasional alcohol.
Home medications per admission reconciliation: psyllium daily, ibuprofen 400 mg every 6-8 h as needed (chronic), albuterol HFA as needed, polyethylene glycol 3350 as needed.
Allergies: NKDA. History of TRALI.

Admission exam: BP 122/78, HR 96, RR 20, SpO2 94% on room air. Reflexes diminished throughout all four limbs. Strength reduced in the legs. No muscle tenderness, no fasciculations. Remainder of examination unremarkable.

Course:
- Lumbar puncture 05/07: CSF protein 112 mg/dL with 2 white cells/uL (albuminocytologic dissociation).
- NCS/EMG 05/08: acute demyelinating sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
- Respiratory: admitted to the neuro ICU for serial vital capacity; lowest FVC 2.4 L. Never required intubation or noninvasive ventilation.
- Treatment: IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (05/07-05/11). Tolerated well.
- Transferred to the ward 05/11. Weakness plateaued then began to improve.

Discharge: to inpatient rehabilitation 05/15. Follow-up neurology in about 8 weeks. PCP after rehab discharge.

documents.title: Call with inpatient team
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hospital neurology resident called as a courtesy - Phil admitted 5/7 with Guillain-Barré, finished IVIG yesterday, out of the ICU, breathing numbers stayed OK. Planning acute rehab. Gave them his med list from here (acetaminophen, not ibuprofen; ibuprofen stopped 2024) and the TRALI history. They will send the summary.

documents.title: Inpatient rehabilitation discharge summary
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
INPATIENT REHABILITATION DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/15/2026, discharged 05/29/2026.
Diagnosis: Guillain-Barré syndrome (AIDP) after IVIG.
Program: daily PT and OT. Leg and grip strength improved through the stay. Transfers independent. Ambulating household and short community distances with a rolling walker; stairs with rail and supervision.
Discharged home with a rolling walker. Outpatient physical therapy recommended. Neurology follow-up as scheduled.
Medications at discharge: psyllium daily, acetaminophen 500 mg 1-2 tabs every 6 h as needed, albuterol HFA as needed, polyethylene glycol 3350 as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

orders.reason: Guillain-Barré syndrome, gait and strength rehabilitation

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Guillain-Barré, AIDP. Neuro ICU 5/7-5/11 (IVIG x5 days, no intubation, lowest FVC 2.4 L), ward to 5/15, inpatient rehab 5/15-5/29. Both summaries reviewed.

How he is: home 11 days. Walks in the house with the walker, some steps without it holding the counter. Feet still tingle. Hands better - can button his shirt. Breathing fine; the April chest cold is long gone. Doing the rehab home exercises. Bowels OK with fiber/PEG.
Smoking: says he barely smoked in the hospital, back to smoking at home. Talked about it; he's still not ready for a medication.

Med rec: psyllium, acetaminophen PRN, albuterol PRN, PEG PRN. Hospital list had him on chronic ibuprofen - that's an old entry; he has not been prescribed it since 2024. Corrected with him.

Vitals reviewed. Wt 95 kg. Lungs: no wheeze. Heart regular. Neuro: reflexes reduced at knees and ankles. Leg strength reduced bilaterally. Gets up from the chair using his arms. Walks with a rolling walker, steady.

A/P
1. GBS, recovering - outpatient PT referral placed today. Neurology follow-up 7/14. Reviewed warning signs (worsening weakness, trouble breathing or swallowing) - go to the ED.
2. Acute bronchitis - resolved.
3. Lung ca - oncology surveillance CT moved from May because of the admission; they will reschedule.
4. Labs today: CBC, CMP.
RTC 6-8 weeks, sooner prn.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY CLINIC
Visit 07/14/2026

Guillain-Barré syndrome (AIDP), onset early May, treated with IVIG.
Interval: steady gains with outpatient PT. Now walking with a single-point cane outside, nothing at home. Residual tingling in the toes. No breathing or swallowing issues.
Exam: strength improved in both legs, not yet full. Reflexes still reduced at the knees and ankles. Gait with cane steady.
Plan: continue PT. Recovery may continue for months. Return in 3 months, sooner if any new weakness.
Allergies: NKDA.
